messages:
Incidents Bot: ALERT: p95 latency > 2s for /v1/generate in prod (us-west-2) — spikes started ~2024-11-02T12:05:14Z, sustained. Incident ID INC-2105-01
PagerDuty Bot: paging Olivia (Oncall) — escalation to SRE
Olivia (Oncall): on it. pulling up grafana + traces. assigning to Sara as lead SRE. tagging @dan @mike for infra/runtime context.
Sara (SRE): joining. quick status — are we seeing errors or just latency?
Olivia (Oncall): no 5xx flood, error rate flat. p50 barely moved, p95 jumped from ~350ms -> ~1.9s. throughput similar.
Dan (Infra): pushed kernel update to inference nodes at 12:03 (rolling, explicit kernel-6.6.2-rc1). can roll back if needed but need careful drain.
Mike (Runtime): noted some tail latency on nodes with newer kernel in canary earlier today but small. can we map which hosts are higher p95?
Olivia (Oncall): correlating now — 12:05-12:12 window shows host set a,b,c with kernel 6.6 are top offenders. sending host list.
Olivia (Oncall): hosts: gpu-uw2-12, gpu-uw2-14, gpu-uw2-19
Sara (SRE): pulling perf counters + top-like stats. starting with `pidstat -C inference` and `perf top` capture.
Sara (SRE): sending quick log excerpts:
```
2024-11-02T12:06:02Z gpu-uw2-12 runtime[pid=4211]: request id=... lat=2120ms tokens=324
2024-11-02T12:06:03Z kernel: task runtime invoked oom-killer? (no) page_fault: major=1
2024-11-02T12:07:10Z runtime: kv_cache_miss key=... duration=18ms
```
Mike (Runtime): interesting — kv_cache_miss durations are fine. but there are long kernel_page_fault spans in traces. grabbing jaeger spans now.
Tracing Bot: long span detected: kernel_page_fault (duration 1.5s) tag: host=gpu-uw2-12, trace_id=0x8f3a...
Leo (ML Eng): could this be disk-backed swap or IO contention? our models try to keep KV cache in RAM but maybe kernel reclaim path triggered.
Dan (Infra): no swap configured on these nodes. but we enabled aggressive THP defrag yesterday via sysctl change: vm.compact_memory=1 on canary pool. rolling change at 12:01-12:04.
Sara (SRE): hypothesis A: kernel memory compaction/hugepage/THP activity causing long stop-the-world kernel page fault delays on some workloads -> p95 tail. hypothesis B: scheduling/context-switch regression in 6.6.2 leading to softirq stalls under steady GPU DMA patterns.
Jess (PM): customer impact? which customers hit the p95? any big SLAs?
Olivia (Oncall): impact table from quick query (12:05-12:20): 47 tenant keys saw p95>1s. top impacted: search-pipeline, support-bot. No quota errors, just latency.
Sara (SRE): mitigation attempt 1: cordon/gdrain gpu-uw2-12 and divert traffic -> observed p95 drop cluster-wide by ~200ms but still above baseline.
Mike (Runtime): mitigation attempt 2: enable per-request fallback to alternative model variant (smaller KV footprint) for impacted routes via routing policy — rolled to 10% of traffic to reduce tail. helped reduce customer visible p95 by ~300ms on affected tenants.
Dan (Infra): immediate rollback candidate: revert vm.compact_memory change on canary hosts. can test on one host (gpu-uw2-19) and watch.
Olivia (Oncall): run revert on gpu-uw2-19 now? say go/no-go.
Sara (SRE): go. reverting sysctl on gpu-uw2-19 to previous value (0).
Sara (SRE): revert applied at 12:29:11Z on gpu-uw2-19. metrics: host p95 dropped from 1.9s -> 620ms over 3 min.
Dan (Infra): confirming: hosts still with vm.compact_memory=1 have worse p95. initial correlation looks strong.
Mike (Runtime): traces for reverted host show kernel_page_fault spans now <=120ms, before they were ~1.2s. attaching trace snippets: 
```
# before (gpu-uw2-12)
span: kernel_page_fault duration=1187ms
span: runtime_dispatch duration=20ms
# after revert (gpu-uw2-19)
span: kernel_page_fault duration=82ms
span: runtime_dispatch duration=18ms
```
Leo (ML Eng): sounds like compaction path caused large latencies for some workloads under our memory pattern. how many hosts got the sysctl?
Dan (Infra): 12 hosts in canary pool received the change; 3 of them now show >1s p95.
Sara (SRE): decision: roll back vm.compact_memory change across canary pool immediately and keep nodes cordoned until stabilized. will schedule controlled rollback for Dedicated pools after testing.
Jess (PM): pinging affected customers with status update. will include mitigation + rollback plan.
Olivia (Oncall): running timeline so far:
- 12:01 - vm.compact_memory=1 applied to canary pool (rolling)
- 12:03 - kernel 6.6.2 rolled to same canary hosts (overlapped)
- 12:05 - p95 latency spike first observed
- 12:06-12:20 - traces show long kernel_page_fault spans on subset of hosts
- 12:29 - reverted sysctl on gpu-uw2-19 -> p95 improved
- 12:35 - mitigation: route 10% to smaller model variants to reduce exposure
- 12:48 - started rollback across remaining canary hosts (in progress)

Sara (SRE): immediate follow-ups for RCA thread:
- collect perf counters (page-faults/sec, context-switches, softirqs) from affected vs unaffected hosts for the window.
- collect kernel config diff and audit who/why compact_memory changed.
- run micro-reproduction with model workload to reproduce compaction delay.
- check whether GPU DMA patterns correlate with pages being reclaimed (large contiguous allocations?)
Mike (Runtime): I'll instrument more fine-grained KV cache metrics and add a tag for host kernel version + sysctl to traces so future correlation is easier.
Dan (Infra): I'll open infra-PR to add a rollout gating check: don't toggle vm.compact_memory without a perf smoke test.
Tracing Bot: attached link: https://tracing.internal/trace/0x8f3a... (redacted) — long kernel_page_faults flagged.
Leo (ML Eng): for RCA hypothesis testing I'd like to run a synthetic workload that induces heavy page churn and measure compaction latency under 6.6.2 vs 6.5 with/without vm.compact_memory. I'll coordinate in eng-ml channel.
Sara (SRE): tagging follow-on owners: Dan -> infra rollout gating; Mike -> runtime tracing tags + small model routing; Leo -> repro; Jess -> customer comms.
Olivia (Oncall): current status: partial rollback in progress, customer-visible p95 improved by ~45% since mitigations. keeping incident open until full rollback and 2h stabilization.
Jess (PM): drafting status, will share to #support and ramp comms.
Sara (SRE): adding final notes to thread: initial root-cause candidate = interaction between vm.compact_memory=1 compaction behavior and kernel 6.6 series + our memory allocation pattern for KV cache, causing long kernel page-fault/compaction stop-the-world latencies on subset of hosts. next: reproduce, collect counters, and harden rollout process.
Olivia (Oncall): thanks all. will hand this to normal RCA process once stabilized. @Incidents Bot please mark incident as "mitigated" when rollback done on all canary hosts. :white_check_mark:
Incidents Bot: acknowledged — will update INC record and create RCA draft ticket assigned to Sara.
Sara (SRE): signing off on real-time mitigation. will file formal RCA with timeline, perf dumps, trace ids, and PR refs.
Jess (PM): +1. closing loop once RCA published. :thumbsup:
